hints.title: Tree Matching Problem
hints.text: Selecting edges such that no two chosen edges share a vertex is the maximum weight matching problem on a tree.

hints.title: Subtree State Definition
hints.text: For each node u, compute two values: max score in u's subtree without choosing any edge incident to u, and max score choosing at most one incident edge to u.

hints.title: Child Edge Optimization
hints.text: If no edge to u's children is chosen, sum max scores of all children. If edge (u, v, w) is chosen, gain is w plus v's score without incident edges.

hints.title: Tree Dynamic Programming Matching Implementation

variables: n: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Single post-order DFS traversal across tree nodes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all edge combinations takes exponential 2^n time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency list and call stack require linear space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models tree maximum weight matching using two-state subtree dynamic programming.
